profile.campus: Cincinnati/Hamilton, Butler County, Ohio (CyrusOne CIN4 campus)
profile.reading:
Per a datacenterHawk listing dedicated to the CIN4 site code (CyrusOne's own stored CIN4 URL returned a 404 on a fresh fetch this session), this facility sits at 103 Knightsbridge Drive, Cincinnati, OH; no sqft or MW figure was located for this specific building this session.

This facility is part of CyrusOne's Cincinnati-metro cluster, the company's home market: Wikipedia's CyrusOne entry states Cincinnati Bell purchased a stake in CyrusOne for $525 million in 2010 and divested it in 2015 after CyrusOne's 2013 IPO; the company was originally founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, and was taken private again in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) acquired it for approximately $15 billion. The Cincinnati cluster spans buildings in Cincinnati proper, Lebanon, and Butler and Warren Counties in Ohio, plus a related facility across the Ohio River in Florence, Kentucky, reflecting the metro's historical role as CyrusOne's founding market before the company's national and international expansion.

Ohio's Cincinnati metro sits within the PJM Interconnection regional transmission grid, and Duke Energy is the dominant electric utility serving the Cincinnati area; PJM has separately flagged rising data center electricity demand across its multi-state footprint (which spans much of the Mid-Atlantic and Midwest, including Northern Virginia's much larger concentration of facilities) as a factor in its long-term capacity planning. Cincinnati's relatively central US location, moderate climate, and status as CyrusOne's founding home market, rather than proximity to any single hyperscale anchor tenant, are what have kept the company concentrating multiple buildings in this metro even as its larger growth in recent years has shifted toward Texas, Virginia, and international markets.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Cincinnati-Hamilton CIN4 is located in Butler County, Ohio. The operator has not published IT capacity or power specifications for this facility. Without published figures for power draw or rack density, the campus cannot be placed against the state's 60.4 MW of published data center capacity or ranked among Ohio's eight facilities with disclosed specifications.

Ohio has 76 mapped data center facilities, of which only eight have published power figures in this registry. CIN4 is not among the eight disclosed facilities, making it one of the 68 Ohio data centers whose capacity remains unmeasured in public sources.

CyrusOne is a large-scale operator acquired by KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners in 2021 and now privately held. Whether this Cincinnati site matters to AI scaling depends on information the operator has chosen not to publish: the power available to the facility, the fraction allocated to compute, and the timeline for expansion. These facts determine whether CIN4 represents committed capacity, planned capacity, or a legacy facility with no bearing on near-term AI infrastructure growth.
